knowledge:
- key_parameters: x=A data frame containing sample metadata or a phenoData slot of an ExpressionSet ;; optimal=A character vector of variable names in the sample metadata to be optimized across batches ;; strata=A character vector of variable names to be blocked during the block randomization step ;; plate=A predefined plate layout object (e.g., IlluminaBeadChip96Plate) or a custom BeadPlate object ;; n=The number of plates/batches in the container ;; batch=The level at which batch effects are controlled, typically 'plates' or 'chips' ;; exclude=A data frame specifying plates, chips, and wells to be excluded from sample assignment ;; fun=The optimization algorithm to use, either "optimal.shuffle" (default) or "optimal.block" ;; nSim=The number of simulations/shuffling attempts (commonly 5000 or more in practice)
- alternatives: Complete Random Design (CRD) is a simple randomization alternative, but the documentation warns it has a high probability of introducing statistically significant batch confounding. Within OSAT, "optimal.shuffle" (default) blocks all variables first and then shuffles, whereas "optimal.block" blocks only specified strata variables and optimizes the rest (slower but guarantees perfect blocking on primary variables).
- when_to_use: Use OSAT during the experimental design phase before running high-throughput genomics assays (e.g., microarrays, RNA-seq, methylation) to assign clinical/biological samples to physical plates, chips, or wells, especially when sample collections are unbalanced or incomplete.
- pitfalls: Avoid filling batches sequentially and leaving empty wells at the end of the last plate, as this creates a highly distinct batch; instead, let OSAT distribute empty wells randomly. Do not use too few simulations (nSim should be 5000+ in practice). Be aware of the trade-off when using "optimal.block": prioritizing the primary variable perfectly will sacrifice the uniformity of other optimized confounding variables.

workflows.name: standard_sample_assignment
workflows.intent: Optimize sample-to-batch assignment across multiple plates using the default shuffle algorithm to minimize batch effects for all variables.
input: samples.txt (Tab-delimited text file containing sample metadata with biological and confounding variables)
workflows.stages: 1. Load sample metadata ;; 2. Define sample setup with variables to optimize ;; 3. Define container setup (plates and batch level) ;; 4. Create optimized setup using the default shuffle algorithm ;; 5. Export the optimized assignment to a CSV file ;; 6. Map the design to a robotic loader layout and export ;; 7. Perform quality control visualization and statistical testing
workflows.code:
library(OSAT)
inPath <- system.file('extdata', package='OSAT')
pheno <- read.table(file.path(inPath, 'samples.txt'), 
                    header=TRUE, sep="\t", colClasses="factor")
gs <- setup.sample(pheno, optimal=c("SampleType", "Race", "AgeGrp"))
gc <- setup.container(IlluminaBeadChip96Plate, 6, batch='plates')
set.seed(123)
gSetup <- create.optimized.setup(sample=gs, container=gc, nSim=1000)
write.csv(get.experiment.setup(gSetup), 
          file="gSetup.csv", row.names=FALSE)
out <- map.to.MSA(gSetup, MSA4.plate)
write.csv(out, "MSAsetup.csv", row.names = FALSE)
QC(gSetup)

workflows.name: prioritized_blocking_assignment
workflows.intent: Optimize sample-to-batch assignment prioritizing a primary biological variable (blocking) while optimizing other confounding variables.
input: samples.txt (Tab-delimited text file containing sample metadata with biological and confounding variables)
workflows.stages: 1. Load sample metadata ;; 2. Define sample setup specifying the primary variable as strata and all variables as optimal ;; 3. Define container setup ;; 4. Create optimized setup using the "optimal.block" algorithm ;; 5. Perform quality control visualization and statistical testing
workflows.code:
library(OSAT)
inPath <- system.file('extdata', package='OSAT')
pheno <- read.table(file.path(inPath, 'samples.txt'), 
                    header=TRUE, sep="\t", colClasses="factor")
gs2 <- setup.sample(pheno,  strata=c("SampleType"), 
          optimal=c("SampleType", "Race", "AgeGrp") )
gc <- setup.container(IlluminaBeadChip96Plate, 6, batch='plates')
set.seed(123)
gSetup2 <- create.optimized.setup("optimal.block", 
          sample=gs2, container=gc, nSim=1000)
QC(gSetup2)

workflows.name: paired_sample_assignment
workflows.intent: Assign paired samples (e.g., pre- and post-treatment specimens from the same individual) to the same chip to eliminate chip-level batch effects on treatment differences.
input: samples.txt (Tab-delimited text file containing sample metadata with biological and confounding variables)
workflows.stages: 1. Load sample metadata ;; 2. Define sample setup with primary and confounding variables ;; 3. Define custom mock chip and plate layouts to represent pairs ;; 4. Define container setup using the mock plate ;; 5. Assign pairs to mock chip rows using "optimal.block" ;; 6. Expand mock layout to real 2-column BeadChip layout ;; 7. Shuffle specimens within chips to avoid location bias ;; 8. Perform quality control visualization and statistical testing
workflows.code:
library(OSAT)
inPath <- system.file('extdata', package='OSAT')
pheno <- read.table(file.path(inPath, 'samples.txt'), 
                    header=TRUE, sep="\t", colClasses="factor")
gs <- setup.sample(pheno, optimal=c("SampleType", "Race", "AgeGrp"),
           strata=c("SampleType"))
newChip <- new("BeadChip",  nRows=6, nColumns=1, byrow=FALSE, 
   comment="mock chip")
newPlate <- new("BeadPlate", chip=newChip,
   nRows=2L, nColumns=4L, 
   comment="mock plate")
gcNew <- setup.container(newPlate, 12, batch="plates")
set.seed(12345)
gPaired <- create.optimized.setup("optimal.block", sample=gs, 
           container=gcNew, nSim=1000)
set.seed(456)
out1 <- get.experiment.setup(gPaired)
out1$Replica <- FALSE
idx <- sample(nrow(out1), ceiling(nrow(out1)/2), replace=FALSE)
out1[idx, "Replica"] <- TRUE
out2 <- out1
out2$columns <- 2
out2$wells <- out2$wells+6
out2$Replica <- !out1$Replica
out3 <- rbind(out1, out2)
idx1 <- with(out3, order(plates, chips,  rows, columns, wells))
out3 <- out3[idx1,]
set.seed(789)
idx2 <- with(out3, order(plates, chips, runif(nrow(out3))))
out4 <- cbind(out3[, 1:8], out3[idx2, 9:11], Replica=out3[, 12])
idx3 <- with(out4, order(plates,  chips, wells))
out4 <- out4[idx3,]
multi.barplot(out3, grpVar='plates', varList=c("SampleType", "Replica", 
              "Race", "AgeGrp"), main="paired sample")
multi.chisq.test(out3, grpVar='plates', varList=c("SampleType", "Replica", 
              "Race", "AgeGrp"))
